claims.statement: For k>=3, epsilon_k=2^-k, and the biased Boolean gate g_k(X,Y)=(-1)^(XY) with iid Bernoulli(epsilon_k) inputs, the B09 restriction gain J_k and M_k=H(S_X|S_Y) satisfy J_k>=r_k(k-log2(e)) and M_k<=r_k epsilon_k(4k+2log2(e)), where r_k=4epsilon_k^2(1-epsilon_k). Hence J_k/(2r_k+M_k) diverges. Encoding X,Y as ANDs of k fair bits gives an actual uniform Boolean point defect f_k with exact M_code=M_k+r_k log2(2^k-1), I(f_k)=2r_k k2^(k-1)/(2^k-1), and H(f_k)/I(f_k)->4. With N_k=2^(2k) disjoint copies per scale, the collapsed biased helper ratio diverges linearly while the actual uniform tower has H/I->4.
claims.quantifiers: All integers k>=3; tower depth K>=3; all physical coordinates of distinct copies are disjoint.
scope_exclusions: Not a counterexample to uniform FEI.
Does not rule out a biased restriction inequality with the B09 endpoint tax.
Does not address overlapping or correlated auxiliary encodings.
refutes: Every fixed-constant tax-free product-biased helper J <= C(I_core+M)
